newsitem.title: USA: Glickman says hopes to unveil CRP rules next week.
newsitem.headline: Glickman says hopes to unveil CRP rules next week.

text.p: U.S. Department of Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said he hoped to announce new proposed rules for the Conservation Reserve Program next week.
"We hope it will be next week. I think people will find the rules fair," Glickman told reporters at the National Cattlemen's Beef Association annual convention here.
Earlier this week Rep. Bob Smith (R), chairman of the House Agriculture Committee, said the CRP issue needed to be resolved quickly as some land was due to come out of the program by March 1.
"We have a 60-day waiting period (for comment). Hopefully we can suspend that," Smith said.
Under CRP, farmers enroll acreage that must be managed under strict soil conservation and wildlife habitat rules in exchange for government payments.
